_note: Verified entries were each confirmed against an official government source (legal text or official status page) as enacted AND in force — worldwide audit of Oct 1, 2026. 'unverified' entries are reported by secondary sources but not yet confirmed on an official government site; they are shown separately with an Unverified badge and must be confirmed before promotion.

laws.name: Artificial Intelligence Act — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
laws.summary: The world's first comprehensive AI law: risk-tiered rules (prohibited / high-risk / transparency duties), conformity assessments for high-risk systems, and obligations for general-purpose AI models. Phased application through 2027–2028.

laws.name: Interim Measures for the Management of Generative AI Services
laws.summary: Requires generative AI services offered to the Chinese public to align with socialist values, complete security assessments and algorithm filings before launch, and respect IP and personal-information protections. Issued jointly by the CAC and six other regulators.

laws.name: AI Basic Act (Framework Act on AI Development and Establishment of Trust)
laws.summary: Consolidated 19 prior bills into Asia's first comprehensive AI framework. Risk-based duties for 'high-impact' AI (impact assessments, human oversight), generative-output labeling, and extraterritorial reach; fines up to KRW 30 million.

laws.name: AI Promotion Act (Act No. 53 of 2025)
laws.summary: Japan's first AI-specific national law. Innovation-first: no fines or penalties — the government may issue guidance, request information, or publicly name non-compliant entities. Established an AI Strategy Headquarters.

laws.name: Texas Responsible AI Governance Act (TRAIGA), HB 149
laws.summary: Comprehensive state AI statute: prohibits AI used to manipulate behavior, enable unlawful discrimination, or generate CSAM; bans government social scoring; creates a 36-month regulatory sandbox and AI advisory council. Enforced exclusively by the Texas AG.

laws.name: Connecticut AI Responsibility and Transparency (CART) Act, SB 5
laws.summary: Omnibus state AI law: anti-discrimination rules for automated employment decision tools, deployer disclosure duties, AI subscription and chatbot provisions, and whistleblower protections for frontier-AI developers. Notice requirements phase in through 2028.

laws.name: TAKE IT DOWN Act (Public Law 119-12)
laws.summary: Federal law criminalizing knowing publication of authentic or AI-generated nonconsensual intimate imagery; requires covered platforms to establish a notice-and-removal process with 48-hour removal on valid request.

laws.name: AI Policy Act (SB 149)
laws.summary: First U.S. state law specifically regulating generative AI: requires disclosure when consumers interact with AI (on request generally, proactively in regulated occupations), establishes liability for AI-driven consumer-protection violations, and creates an Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy. Amended by SB 226 (effective May 7, 2025).

laws.name: Transparency in Frontier AI Act (SB 53)
laws.summary: Requires large frontier-AI developers to publish safety and security frameworks, report critical safety incidents to the state, and implement whistleblower protections; the industry-backed successor to the vetoed SB 1047.

laws.name: Provisions on the Administration of Algorithm Recommendation in Internet Information Services
laws.summary: China's foundational algorithm regulation (joint CAC/MIIT/MPS/SAMR order): requires algorithm filing with the CAC, user disclosure and opt-out of algorithmic recommendations, non-discrimination, and protections for minors, the elderly, and gig workers; covers generation-synthesis (deepfake) algorithms alongside recommenders.

laws.name: General Data Protection Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2016/679), Article 22
laws.summary: Article 22 gives individuals the right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produce legal or similarly significant effects, with exceptions and safeguards such as human intervention.

laws.name: Product Liability Directive (Directive (EU) 2024/2853)
laws.summary: Modernizes EU no-fault product liability and expressly treats software, including AI systems, as 'products,' naming AI system providers as manufacturers; member-state transposition due by December 2026.

laws.name: Artificial Intelligence in Government Act of 2020 (P.L. 116-260)
laws.summary: Created the GSA AI Center of Excellence and directed OMB guidance on federal agencies' acquisition and use of AI.

laws.name: National Artificial Intelligence Initiative Act of 2020 (P.L. 116-283)
laws.summary: Established the National AI Initiative and its coordination office to accelerate and coordinate federal AI research and development.

laws.name: Advancing American AI Act (P.L. 117-263)
laws.summary: Requires OMB guidance on agency AI use, AI safeguards in federal contracts, and public inventories of agency AI use cases.

laws.name: Executive Order 14179 — Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence
laws.summary: Revoked EO 14110 and directed development of an AI Action Plan plus revised OMB guidance on federal AI governance.

laws.name: Executive Order 14365 — Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence
laws.summary: Directs the Attorney General to create an AI Litigation Task Force to challenge state AI laws and moves toward a national AI policy framework.

laws.name: Illinois HB 3773 / Public Act 103-0804
laws.summary: Makes it a civil rights violation for employers to use AI with a discriminatory effect in employment decisions or to use zip codes as a proxy for protected classes; requires notice to employees of AI use.

laws.name: New York City Local Law 144 of 2021 (Automated Employment Decision Tools)
laws.summary: Requires independent bias audits and public summaries, plus advance notice to candidates and employees, when automated employment decision tools are used in hiring.

laws.name: Directive on Automated Decision-Making (Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat)
laws.summary: Requires federal institutions to complete algorithmic impact assessments, give notice and explanations, test and monitor automated systems, and provide human intervention and recourse; compliance required by April 1, 2020.

laws.name: Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis of Internet Information Services (Order No. 12)
laws.summary: Requires real-identity verification, labeling of deep-synthesis (deepfake) content, algorithm filing, and security assessments for deep synthesis service providers.

laws.name: Measures for the Labeling of AI-Generated Synthetic Content
laws.summary: Requires explicit (visible) and implicit (metadata) labeling of AI-generated synthetic content and bans malicious removal or falsification of labels.

laws.name: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, section 80
laws.summary: Replaces UK GDPR Article 22 with Articles 22A–22D: solely automated 'significant decisions' require safeguards including information, the right to make representations, human intervention, and the right to contest.
